system.summary: Two-part 3-figure codes of about 900 (1719) and 800 (1742-45) groups mixing words, syllables and letters.
system.notes: Two-part inferred from the 1719 glosses: re 36, pas 88, le 95, que 184, vous 243, a 347 are not alphabetical. Carré 1742-45: 1323 groups, 381 distinct, values 1-800; letter-homophonic anneal no better than the shuffled control; one-part test r=-0.26 against an alphabetical French word list, so two-part.

prior_solution.where: contemporary interlinear glosses on R2964/R2965; R2963 and R2974 fully deciphered at the time

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched all images of R2963-R2974 with the DECODE cookie.
BL catalogue (unidentified cipher keys) and web search for the shelfmark; no edition.
Identified each record: R2963, R2966, R2967, R2971, R2973, R2974 deciphered at the time; R2969 a frequency count, not a key.
R2964 transcribed in full with the glosses.
354 groups, 191 distinct, 116 singletons, max 900; glosses not alphabetical, so a two-part code.
One-part (alphabetical) code, which would let the glosses bracket the rest.
Fetched R2968, R2969, R2972 images with the DECODE cookie (R2970 already held).
Transcribed all three letters from full-resolution images (1323 groups).
Compared counts with the contemporary tally R2969 (= R2968+R2970 incl. a dittography): 22 of 25 values exact, 3 off by one.
381 distinct of 1323, 147 singletons, range 1-800, top value 2.3%; one repeated 5-gram; 73% of 1745 tokens use 1742 values.
Same anneal on shuffled ciphertext scores the same (-2.12/-2.17 v -2.09/-2.11 per char).
One-part (alphabetical) code: band-mass correlation with an alphabetical French word list r=-0.26; top values no closer to function-word positions than random.

Key hunt for the Carré code: viewed R2971 (different 4-figure code, to a prince, not Carré; its de=448/que=745 absent from the Carré text) and R2975-R2981 (1749-59 letter ciphers/codes, none in the Carré code); R2972 pencil marks shown to be sheet cross-references to recurring runs, not decipherments; web search for Carré, Pall Mall, the jeweller Chevening and Add MS 32305 found nothing.
Catalogue #79 (R2978-R2979, 'Unknown sender (Dresden)'): fetched both records' images (4 + 2 pp.) with the DECODE cookie.

R2978 (f. 32, Dresden 25 Jan 1750): 2-figure letter cipher deciphered letter by letter between the lines at the time (names Mr de Guydickens). R2979 (f. 34, Hague 9 Aug 1753, 'Hanau to Fer.'): the decipherer's working copy of a 4-figure syllable/word code, glossed in part, question marks where he stopped. Closed as read at the time / read in part at the time; no new decipherment attempted.

outcome.method_basis: The Paris 1719 and Carre 1742-45 letters are two-part codes; only the contemporary interlinear glosses on R2964/R2965 give values, and the three Carre letters (1,323 groups) were transcribed and tested without a reading.
outcome.notes: fraction_read counts the contemporary glosses in R2964 (33 of 354 groups). Needs a key, a clear copy or many more letters in the same code. The Carré letters (R2968/R2970/R2972) were transcribed in full (1323 groups) and tested; not read.
